newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican same-day peso closes 2.6 centavos firmer.
newsitem.headline: Mexican same-day peso closes 2.6 centavos firmer.

text.p: Mexico's same-day peso closed firmer against the dollar on Monday after a dull session and on expectations of a strengthening Cetes market, traders said.

"I haven't seen very much activity all morning...maybe some banks dumping costly long (dollar) positions and the odd foreign investor picking up government paper in case rates fall tomorrow," a trader said, referring to the primary Cetes auction.

The same-day peso closed 2.6 centavos firmer at 7.5340/7.5380 per dollar. Same-day trades, which close early, had lagged behind late trading in 24-hour and 48-hour trading late Friday, in which the peso recouped ground lost against the dollar.
Meanwhile, 24-hour and 48-hour contracts were 1.55 and 1.30 centavos firmer at 7.5390/7.5425 and 7.5440/7.5470 per dollar, respectivamente.
Currency traders said that 24-hour and 48-hour peso contracts may recede a little in later trading if Mexican stocks slide further.
"The bolsa is a little erratic despite the bullish Dow Jones and forecasts, albeit somewhat unclear ones, that primary rates will fall," a peso trader said.
The blue-chip IPC index of Mexican stocks was 8.41 points down, or 0.25 percent, at 3332.52.
